answer: Non-kin attestation quorums resist sybils: an identity counts only once enough established, UNRELATED peers vouch for it, and self-referential rings are discounted. A fake cluster is a closed island that only mirrors itself, earning nothing — each pulse of its vouching bounces back inward. Honest identities gather many independent vouches from the wider graph; a ring has only its own reflection, so the counting rule starves it however large it grows.
